We shall skip over 27, it is quite illegible, and we shall proceed, move on to document 28. Please, can you tell me this: You said that Jasmin Jaganjac was sent by Mr. Tudjman, right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that he was defence adviser to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later, when he ceased being an officer, a major of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He was accepted by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic irrespective of his background, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Izetbegovic, like all of us, tried to find persons in close contact with the Croats in order to establish an active and sound relationship with them. And, of course, from that standpoint, and I have to expand because you asked me that --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise. Just one minute. You had no contact with Mr. Izetbegovic except for a meeting in November, as you said before. So can you talk about things that you know without inferring any conclusions from what somebody else might have said. I'm just asking you, is it a fact that Jasmin Jaganjac was defence advisor to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic? I'm asking you this question because here you have an order, and if we scroll this document up - you can see it but we cannot - it was signed by Jasmin Jaganjac, was it not? As there is no translation, I shall translate it. I shall have items 1 and 2 translated for the benefit of everybody in the courtroom. This is from the 6th of June, 1992, to send 11 combatants to the unit commanded by Semsudin Masic, to the Raska Gora Dubrani area. The leader of the group is Mafija Catic, is that correct? Is that what this document states?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We shall move on immediately because I'm using up a lot of time and there are so many counts to cover, so many points to cover. The second document is 2D 00029. Let us immediately move on. This is a command, an order, is it not, also signed by Jasmin Jaganjac? Item 1 says, "To the officer Ibro Halilagic is to be assigned as chief commander, Commander-in-Chief of the tactical group in the Feteci [phoen] area." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, I'll have you comment at the end but let us just go through these documents. Would you please confirm who is within the structure in this -- would you not agree that there were commanding staff among the structure of these forces, because you said that they were only marginalised. Can I ask the usher to return to the screen 2D 00028. That's right. Just focus on the stamps. What stamps does this document bear?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Independent Defence Battalion, Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you just tell the Trial Chamber what the coats of arms inside the stamp are.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this stamp, there is the coat of arms of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and of the Croatian Defence Council, but this is something that you are seeking to argument --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, please. Bear with me.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is of the essence. May I ask the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters. I'm trying to stop the witness. Mr. Smajkic, if you do have a comment, please ask for some time after I am flew. You said what you did, you commented on the coats of arms in the stamps. We just want to place this on record. Let us not comment on the miraculous reasons why they should be there, just let us establish whether they are there.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are there, but I'm asking for the floor from the Trial Chamber because this is not complete information.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Excuse me, I am in charge of this cross-examination at this moment, so if the Trial Chamber feels that it needs to interrupt me, they will certainly do so. Let us go on. Can we put 2D 00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to interfere with cross-examination but I must say that if the witness is not going to be allowed to give what he considers a full answer, the Prosecution will have to come back with a rather extensive and time-consuming redirect examination. I know in the practice in the first part of this trial for the past few weeks, there has been very little, if any - I think only perhaps on one occasion - redirect examination by the Prosecution. But if the witness is not allowed to give what he considers a fair answer, then all I can do is I'm going to go back through his examination -- cross-examination, ask every question again, and give him a chance to give an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. When there are difficulties, I shall intervene myself and I shall pose a question to the witness. We were shown a stamp with the coat of arms of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the left as well as of the Croatian stamp -- coat of arms on the right. Can you explain, and in what way, if you can, can you explain the fact that this document bears a stamp which includes the two sides, the two sides of a coat of arms? Do you have a personal explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is exactly what I was asking for. Please pay attention to this. This is a coat of arms on a document signed by the commander of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Pasalic, meaning that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the desire to establish full communication and cooperation with the Croatian Defence Council, in addition to its own coat of arms with the lilies, it accepts to have also the HVO coat of arms juxtaposed to it. But look at the bottom. The Croatian Defence Council did not want to follow suit and they do not have the lily emblem in their own stamp. So this clearly shows what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Arif Pasalic, as you have just told us, was the commander of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So B and H army commanders have their standard usual stamp, and he affixed that stamp to this document, whereas the -- and that particular stamp says the battalion and refers to the city of Mostar but also contains two coats of arms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has -- the stamp has two coats of arms. One is the one with the lilies and the other is the coat of arms of the Croatian Defence Council. So it is one and the same stamp. Our army always attempted to give equal -- equal -- equal position to the different emblems and the Croatian Defence Council actually opposed that, and this is actually a proper illustration of that, how much we wanted to pursue a solution, because we gladly included the Croatian emblem in our own in order to avoid any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There is something that Mr. Praljak would like to ask.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the coat of arms you have before you, we don't have the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's the Independent Mostar Battalion within the HVO. When the decision was taken to establish the ABiH, they ceased using the coat of arms of Croatia in this joint stamp. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again. I truly am. But was this testimony by Mr. Praljak? There wasn't a question to the witness. Is Mr. Praljak and others just going to pop up at any time and give testimony in the case? I object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you heard Mr. Praljak's personal question. It concerned the fact that there was no BH army but there was a battalion that depended on the HVO. So how would you respond to this question put by Mr. Praljak? Because the Judges have to ask themselves the following: We are told that there is a member of the military called Pasalic who is allegedly a member of the ABiH. We can see the stamp that he has used and we notice that there are two coats of arms within the stamp, and it mentions the Independent Mostar Battalion. As you are someone who was present there at the time, we are asking you for your interpretation. Our question is what is your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I witnessed the events, and I am not supporting either the army or the HVO. I'm speaking in quite objective terms. This document mentions the fact that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is quite prepared to use as part of its stamp the symbols of the Croatian people in order to avoid any conflict, and it's important for me to point this out. Please allow me. From the very beginning, the HVO was against the ABiH. They wanted us to be part of the HVO, whereas we wanted to have our own units but we wanted to fight together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another Judge has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. President, before the Accused Praljak took the floor I wanted to raise the same problem as he did because now we have the letter here in our hands and at the same time, of course, we do not have an English translation, but in the letterhead it is said that HVO Samostalni Bataljon Obrane Mostar, which in my knowledge would mean that it is the Independent unit of the Mostar Battalion. Now, coming back to the original question which was raised, I really believe that, at that time at least, Mr. Arif Pasalic was not, in a way, from the Bosnia-Herzegovina Republic's army but he headed that particular Independent Battalion. So it is my question if it is right or not. And I believe that turning to my colleagues here, and the Presiding Judge and Judge Trechsel, that you have to answer the questions that they are being put to you. So that was my comment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May I continue. With regard to the question just put to you by the Honourable Judge, could we have a closer look at the date of -- on this document, please. The 6th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The ABiH was established at the time. Was -- had it been established by that time? My question is whether the ABiH been established by that time. Whatever you said with regard to the stamp was related to the fact that the HVO didn't recognise the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the ABiH existed at the time. They were involved in fierce fights to liberate the town. In 10 days' time the town was liberated. The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina participated in the liberation of town. It had its own units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. We'll have recourse to other material to prove whether this was the case or not, to prove whether it was the ABiH or what you referred to earlier on. You mentioned the Muslim forces. That wasn't me. There are other questions I will leave to my colleagues who will have a sufficient amount of time to put questions to you about this subject that I now have to skip, but I would now like to move on to another document. You mentioned an agreement in Graz. You elaborated at length on the agreement between Boban and Karadzic. This Trial Chamber has dealt with this agreement. We've already had evidence before us. With your leave, what did Karadzic and Boban agree on? The document concerned is a Prosecution document; P 00192.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps you don't have this document before you. It was admitted into evidence earlier on. Could we have the electronic version on the screen, if possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you have a hard copy, Your Honours, then you have the translation too. It's page 82, or rather, 4 in the electronic version. The number is 2082. It's on page 4. It's a public announcement. And let me provide you another number: L0057801. It's a Prosecution document that was adopted. Do you have the electronic version? It's page 4. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yesterday you told the Prosecution that you were aware of the agreement. Could we just have a look at page number 4. Could we hurry up a little? Could we see the full text to see what this public announcement is. We can see that it relates to the meeting that we are referring to. Could we zoom in to item 1. And item 2. Since we will have this document, my question is, what did Mr. Boban and Karadzic agree on with regard to Mostar? I'll read it out: "In the town of Mostar the Serbian side believes that the border is the Neretva River, whereas the Croatian side believes that the entire town of Mostar is within a Croatian component." So did they agree on anything? That's the text that you referred to yesterday, and you said that it was a Croatian and Serbian agreement. Did they reach any agreement with regard to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen the document before.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Don't mention the field. Would you agree, because you said that you've never seen this document, although you mentioned it yesterday, would you agree with me that they didn't agree on Mostar in any way, if this is the authentic text of the document? I'm discussing the document now.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen the document. However, I mentioned the reactions of the gentlemen who represented Mostar and the HVO. I was present when they discussed the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My question is, if we have a look at the document, and authentic version, the original is in English and this is a translation, that we understand, if we have a look at the document - and I assume the Prosecution will be using this document on numerous other occasions in this courtroom - but my question is very simple: Is this document an authentic one and is this sentence an authentic sentence? Did the Serbs and Croats reach an agreement of any kind about Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, the witness has already testified that he's not seen the document before today, and I specifically took that into account yesterday. I asked the witness was he aware around this time that such an agreement was being discussed? I specifically did not put the document in front of the witness because in fact he had told me that he had not seen the document. So I don't know that he can say anything more about a document to authenticate the document which he says he's never seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't waste any more time. You asked him whether he was familiar with the document. He said that he wasn't. You could then ask him whether he was aware of an agreement between Karadzic and Boban, and he'll just say yes or no. If he says yes, ask him what the agreement was; and if he says no, you may move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Yesterday the witness said that he was aware of this agreement. I am only asking him whether he is familiar with the contents of the agreement. And he even gave his own assessment. He said it was on the basis of this agreement that the Croats didn't go to Eastern Mostar when the town was being liberated. I'm just showing the witness the document he has already referred to. And this is a good sign for the Chamber. If the witness spoke about the document and drew conclusions about the document without having seen the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He quite simply said that this is a document he has never seen. I will solve the problem. You've been following everything. The question put to you by Defence counsel, and I'm putting the same question to you, is as follows: Were you familiar with the contents of agreement, at the time? Not now, but at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the way in which the Croatian authorities acted, we found out that something was happening, and later we have the testimony of Mr. Mesic. This can also be seen in the press. He mentioned this agreement just as the agreement between Tudjman and Milosevic in Karadjordjevo was mentioned, similarly this agreement between Boban and Karadzic in Graz was referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. So may I draw the conclusion that you're talking about dividing Mostar on the basis of a document that you were not familiar with, that you had never seen? Can I draw this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. That's an answer too. Today you were shown certain documents, and in response to a Prosecution question that concerned your correspondence with Bishop Peric, you provided certain answers. I'm not going to go back to the letters that have been admitted into evidence but I would just like to know whether you received a letter from Mr. Ratko Peric dated the 28th of June, 1993. Could we have the document 2D 00012 on the screen. And could the witness say whether he ever received this letter. Could you zoom in a little? And then the witness might be able to tell us whether he has ever seen this letter before, whether he has received this letter -- whether he had received this letter or not. Do you recognise this letter? Did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you received it. Did you also receive all the attachment that the Bishop Ratko Peric refers to in this letters -- in this letter? He mentions a significant number of documents that he attached to this letter.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see which documents are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, if you have a look at page 2 of the B/C/S version of this document, we'll see at the very top of the page some of the documents attached to the letter.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only received the letter, none of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Since you received the letter and since you're familiar with its contents, I will only show you two of the documents referred to in the letter. Could we have the electronic version of document 2D 00021. We have more elements now than in relation to the previous letter. Do you see this order? You see this order was issued on the 19th of April, 1993. It says here the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 1st Mostar Brigade. This is now the full name of this unit; the 1st Mostar Brigade. Have you ever seen this order before, this Order for Defence, that's what it's called.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you received the letter of Bishop Peric, did you inquire about this? Did you attempt to locate it? I will ask you -- I will let you know why I'm asking this. Could we see the previous document, please, Bishop Peric's letter. This is document -- I apologise, just a minute. 2D 00012. Can we just show the second page to the witness, please. The second page, please. The second page of the letter in B/C/S. I'm showing you this page because the bishop, Ratko Peric, refers to this order, and this order is entitled, "The Order for Defence." And as you can see on page 2, under item 5, it says, "I hereby order ..." and we mustn't forget that this order was issued on the 19th of April, 1993. You spoke about the events in May, 1993, and there is why I'm drawing your attention to these portions. So in this document, Bishop Peric brings these extracts from the defence -- from the order, which go as follows: "The 1st Battalion --" I'm reading now under item 5: "The 1st Battalion is tasked with taking defence positions in the sector of South Camp, closing the direction from the village of Rodoc, towards Mostar, in the anti-armour sense. Upon creating conditions for that, move into attack towards the intersection of the roads Mostar-Buna, Mostar-Blagaj." This letter brings several portions of this order based on which you can see that this is actually order for attack. After you received this letter, did you ever attempt to establish whether what Bishop Peric wrote to you about was true? Did you ever look for this document?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I showed no such interest, nor did I know about this. And I don't think that there was any need for me to know about this. I know what the situation was like.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. That's quite sufficient for me. That's quite sufficient. Bishop Ratko Peric enclosed another document when writing to you. This is document 2D 00022. This is quite a lengthy document. While we are waiting for the document, I will tell you that this is the information on the expulsion of Croatian families from Kocani, Grabovica, Malo Polje, Blagaj, which is very important. This is quite a lengthy document, and it gives the names of the expelled persons, those who were expelled from the mentioned local communes. All of these persons are Croats, and then there are also families expelled from the Zdalik [phoen] local community. Mr. Peric referred to this document. Did you ever attempt to inquire whether this was true, this information about the expulsion of Croatian families? This information is dated the 15th of June, 1993. Did you have such information that families were driven out of these areas?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the document but I know for a fact, because I was a protagonist. I didn't take part in expulsions, but I was there in that limited area and I know that these people left not because they were driven out but because they wanted to leave the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. They wanted to leave their homes? How did you establish this, may I ask you that? Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the contact with information who -- on the contact with people who spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who informed you about this? Were they Croats?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The residents of Dracevica and Gnojnica informed me; people living in the areas which these individuals left. They were looking for any possible way to leave that area. I can guarantee you that there was no ethnic cleansing in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Let us try to be as specific as possible. This information that they left their homes voluntarily, did you receive this information precisely from the people who left their homes, from the Croats?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not meet with the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: ... quite a bit of time, and I will now, in conclusion, like to go back to the topic -- I'm nearing the end of my cross-examination. Please tell me this: Among Muslim -- were there any Muslim clerics in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina serving as commanders of units?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please see document 2D 00016, please. Can we see it in e-court, please. You're not the author of this document, but I will ask you whether you can confirm this to me. When I asked you about Muslim clerics, could you tell me whether this is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where was his unit?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had his unit in the area of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we agree that Konjic is a town which was within your jurisdiction, if we can call it that, that it was in the area under your competence?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As I can see, the name was not recorded in the transcript. Let me mention it again slowly. The gentleman's name is Nezir Efendi Halilovic, and his nickname is Muderiz?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is incorrect. It should be Nezim, with M.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. It says here "Nezir" and it should be "Nezim."

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Nezim.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you know when this unit was established? Did you know about its existence?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you consent to this, namely to have clerics take part in the war and play the role of commanders?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nezim Halilovic suspended his official duties during the period of aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina, and he became a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can that be done? Is that allowed in the Islamic religion? Can one suspend his or her function as a cleric, and can they say, "I am no longer a cleric, I'm just a civilian, and then later on I will go back to being a cleric"? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally know Mr. Halilovic and he sincerely wanted this because he was from Zepa, and Zepa is a well-known place where genocide was committed and crimes in Eastern Bosnia. He said then that this was his choice, that he simply could not do anything else but has to give his maximum, devote his utmost efforts to liberating this area. That was his motive. This is why we accepted his resignation to his duties and we accepted that he can become a military person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that he sent a letter of resignation, that you saw that letter, and you agreed to this? You agreed to suspend him as a cleric? You agreed for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are there any rules which regulate this suspension of the religious office? On what did you base your decision to authorise this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We based this, our decision was based on his persistent requests, and his desire to do his utmost. He simply couldn't stand doing anything else while the country was on fire, especially Eastern Bosnia, Srebrenica and Zepa, and that was his native area. He was in Konjic with his work and he wanted to give an active contribution to the liberation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and there was nothing we could do to affect it. We simply complied with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we, based on this, conclude that there are no rules regulating this and that you were guided by his fervent desire and that's what made you accept his request?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We evaluated his case. We saw that he was quite insistent, and that he had an enormous energy that he wanted to invest, to liberate this area occupied by the Jugo army and the Serb forces, that this is what drove him. And he was entitled to resign. He could have resigned and said, "I simply do not wish to work any longer in the Islamic community."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please say who do you mean when you say "we"? You have used this pronoun in plural quite frequently. So I'd like to know who ruled on this, who decided on this?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Islamic community did. He was an employee of the Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was that within your jurisdiction, the jurisdiction of your mufti office or the entire Islamic community? Was that under your jurisdiction or Mr. Ceric's [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a municipal level, so at the level of the Konjic local organs of Islamic community, and at the level of the mufti office for the region of Mostar, and at the level of the entire Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this was a decision that was harmonised at all levels?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something regarding this paragraph. You put a question concerning the 7th paragraph. The 7th paragraph of the document says that in each large town of Bosnia and Herzegovina controlled by the BH army, there was a Jihad unit under the command of Muslim clergy and that this was all under Alija Izetbegovic. This information was provided by the SIS of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw this document, and I don't know everything that was taking place in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As for the role that these special forces had and who they were subordinated to, I don't know what term they used here for them. As for Mr. Halilovic, Muderiz Halilovic, he was commander of the 4th Brigade. That was a brigade which belonged to the corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in our region, in our territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I have just two very brief questions. I lost track of the time. I didn't know that it was almost time for our break.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Today the Presiding Judge asked you something about the book called, "Instructions to an Islamic Fighter." And this is a book referred to by Bishop Peric in his letter to you. Do you know that this brochure or this instructional booklet was distributed to the fighters, to the soldiers in the units of the 4th Corps in the territory where you were, in the region of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that, but it was available.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was available. All right. Did you send any kind of a protest concerning this? Because today, in the courtroom, you said that you did not agree with some of the positions in that booklet, and that in your letters, you gave instructions which are not entirely in compliance with the instructions in this booklet. Did you ever raise this issue? Did you ask that this booklet be withdrawn, and did you ever distance yourself from some of the things mentioned in this booklet?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can give you an answer but I should like to remind the Honourable Trial Chamber that we discussed this subject extensively in the Naletilic and Stela case.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To spare you any further elaboration which will only take your time and mine, forget that case. I asked you a very specific question, and if the Trial Chamber feels that they want to read that particular transcript, they will do so. That is up to the Trial Chamber. I'm asking you, concretely, did you distance yourself from the allegations -- from the -- that book? You told me that you didn't agree with it, that they were distributed in Mostar. I'm simply asking you whether you distanced yourself.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not distributed by my office, my people, but by different military channels, and it was made available and was accessible to people. But I do have to say that one of the Judges in the Stela case had read this case and submitted a report to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please spare me, us, and this Trial Chamber. That is the position of that Trial Chamber, and it is not binding upon anyone. I did not go into the actual content of that text. I didn't condemn it or not condemn it, nor do I have any such intention, or may I do so. I just simply asked you, if you didn't agree with it, did you disassociate yourself from it? You have replied in your peculiar way and we shall now move on. Did there exist the function of Emir in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Have you finished?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have only just started my last set of questions, and I will be through in five minutes, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Then, conclude. You have another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Defence document 2D 0013. Can you zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this your signature, Mr. Smajkic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this a document on the basis of which on the 28th of November, 1992, you were appointing Mimic Ibrahim as Emir of the MS -- those are Muslim forces --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: -- in Mostar until further notice; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is what you said to the Prosecutor yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was done only once?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So that is why I said Muslim forces, quoting you, because I had this document before my eyes and saw that you referred to them as Muslim forces. But the question is not that. It is this: This document states that on the basis of the power of attorney given you, the authorisation given to you, of the chief Emir of the armed forces for Bosnia and Herzegovina from the 25th of November, 1992, issued in Zenica, you were appointing this gentleman the Emir of the Muslim forces, and until now you've been telling me that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not have an Emir in its ranks. Now what is correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Muslim unit in Zenica, a strong unit, and of course it was within the structure of -- the command structure of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it had its Emir. When it was set up in Mostar, that was the very inception of that unit. The problem was who would then appoint that person who, as the Prosecutor yesterday said, would be the chaplain of that unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers please not overlap. The interpreter did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell you now. Mr. Arif Pasalic or somebody else asked me who is going to do this appointing? So I addressed the people in Zenica, and Mr. Mahmut Karalic, who was -- who had that capacity for the 7th Muslim Brigade, he told me that I should be the one to do that. I can recall his very words. He said, "You do that in that area because you know who -- which persons are persons of integrity and could accommodate our needs and our standards."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the post of the chief Emir of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not exist?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not officially.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And unofficially?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how shall I put it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Put it whatever way you like.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit, as I said yesterday, between 40 and 50 men strong, wanted to regulate its daily life in a specific way. And every man fighting for Bosnia and Herzegovina was valuable and we had a differentiated approach to each individual in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sorry, I only have another four minutes before our break. Did there officially or unofficially exist the function of the post of the chief Emir of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly this gentleman introduced himself to me as such but I wasn't aware of an official position of that kind in the army. No, it didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I can conclude that I'm not a graphologist but this is practically identical to your handwriting, so I can conclude that it was your letter, written by you?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I don't have it on the screen any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can the witness again be shown document 2D 00003 -- sorry, 00 -- sorry, 2D 00013.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just a last question: Would you agree with me, and I'm asking you at the end because yesterday you spoke at great length about the desire to establish a joint army, your aspirations, your endeavours, so in this month, in 1992, November, you appointed an Emir. You were aware that there was a cleric in the capacity of a commander and you were aware also of the fact that there was a very pronounced reason for a conflict between the Croatian and the political -- Muslim peoples and political components, in fact. Do you feel that this indeed contributed to the establishment of unity in the troops, of the troops in the army? I'm asking you because you are a cleric yourself and you are very familiar with this. Do you think that this could have been a reason for the mistrust between the factors involved, especially if this was done in an underhand way?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, and I claim, I assert responsibly, that this did not contribute to the conflict between the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am through. I apologise. I must say that you're not talking about -- giving me an answer to my question but you are giving your own comments. Your Honours, if you would please allow me another three minutes after the break? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we bring the witness in, I believe that Mr. Scott wishes to say something in respect of next week's schedule. Please be quick, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now in open session, I have to say that we expect the witness to be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, prior to giving the floor to Madam Nozica for another couple of minutes for her cross-examination, I have to ask you a question so that we could successfully coordinate our work. Tell me, would you perhaps be free next week, to commit yourself to come here on Wednesday? Or perhaps Thursday morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am at the court's disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then it is possible, and as you know, we -- there will be a couple of hours more, and ideally if you could come on Wednesday, it would make it possible for the Defence to finish its cross-examination. So it is possible. Mr. Registrar, please so instruct the WVS unit in order to make all the necessary arrangements. Thank you for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will list the documents that I used. I have to assume that there will be a slight problem with the registrar because some of the problem -- numbers overlap with the documents used by the Prosecution. So would you please be so kind as to later tell me which ones are admitted, but I will read them now in sequence. 2D 00018, 2D 00024, 2D 00025, 26 - always 2Ds and three 0s - 28, 22, 21, 12 -- so 2D 00012 and 16, and, I apologise, 13 also, at the end. And it remains my obligation in respect of the specific documents to submit a translation so that they could be conditionally admitted into the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Registrar, would you please give some thought to this, until the end of today's session. Perhaps there is a part that cannot be admitted for -- because of the lack of a translation into English or French, so we should just give them identification marks but we shall see at the end of the session today. The next counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Smajkic, my name is Bozidar Kovacic, I'm a lawyer from Rijeka. I represent General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, does your client Mr. Praljak have the intention of putting any questions to the witness; and if so, how long does he intend to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I wanted to mention this but I got carried away. Mr. Praljak asked for ten minutes at most, but he will put his questions to the witness after I have cross-examined the witness myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Before the break, my colleague Mrs. Nozica showed you the power of attorney that you yourself had written down, but with regard to document 2D 00013 that we had on the screen, you said in a response you provided on page 66, line 18, of the transcript, that you would now respond to the question: "Mr. Arif Pasalic or someone else asked me who would be responsible for the appointment. I then contacted some people in Zenica, as well as Mr. Mahmut Karalic, who was the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. He was acting in that capacity. And he said that someone had to be made responsible for this. Someone had to do this. I remember those words, and he said in inverted commas, I quote, 'You do that because it concerns your area and these people of integrity who can meet the standards required and comply with the requests.'" So with relation to this matter I'd like to ask you, the 7th Muslim Brigade is a unit that includes mujahedin; is that correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you knew that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The person concerned was the Emir of the 7th Brigade, not the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If you think there is anything you should add, and you've added quite a lot, you can make a sign to the Prosecution who can put the question to you during his re-examination.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is just one word that is important that I would like to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution can put the relevant questions to you. They have the right to do so, and this is a procedure that we have to respect. At the beginning of your testimony yesterday you said that you had already testified in the Naletilic et al. case, and you testified on the 18th and the 19th of October, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'll read out a question put to you by Judge Clark on the 19th of October, 2001: The page in the transcript is 4227. The question was as follows. Obviously there is a part missing in the first sentence. It mentions internationally recognised symbols and then there is a new sentence, and then at the end it has something to do with the war and the instructions to the Muslim fighter. Were those instructions followed when the Islamic faith, within a war context, was at stake. If a soldier is a Muslim, he would be a member of the Islam faith and he would fight together with other Muslims, but the question itself has nothing to do with Islam. It could be something that had to do with a discussion on borders or boundaries or some other matters. I wouldn't want anyone to object to the translation because I'm reading from the original transcript. It might be better if I read out the English transcript and it will be then be adequately translated. Yes, I can see that the judge is making a sign. So this is the text. Judge Clark stated the following: [In English] "Not with those internationally recognised emblems. And then finally, in relation to war and the instructions for the Muslim fighter, do those instructions only apply when the faith of Islam is an issue in the war? If a soldier is a Muslim, he belongs to the Islamic faith, and he is fighting alongside other Muslims but the issue has nothing to do with Islam - it might be a boundary dispute or some such thing - are the same instructions given? Or are those confined to a war with a religious element?" [Interpretation] That was the question put to you. Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many questions were put to me. I can't remember it directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'll now read out the answer you gave to that question, which can be found in the transcript in the Naletilic case the date the 19th of October, 2001, and the page is 4228. I'll now quote your answer in English: [In English] "I am really glad that you put that question to me. I wanted to tell the gentleman, the Defence attorney, something on this subject. These rules that apply to commanders in the sense of their behaviour towards prisoners, that can be applied only in Muslim states where the Sharia law is in force. So this is not binding on us in Bosnia at all. We haven't any Sharia laws according to which these rules would have to be applied. I mean, there are commanders then, and there is a court-martial then, and then that court-martial would have to investigate, and then pass a verdict on liquidation -- I mean, that is not applicable in Bosnia. We recognise the civil laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina." [Interpretation] Mr. Smajkic, that was your answer in the case referred to. Do you accept that as your answer?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Contrary to what we have heard yesterday and today, and contrary to what we have heard with regard to the 7th Muslim Brigade, this different -- this answer is different. Your answers were contradictory, the answers you gave before the same Court. These answers are not identical. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. You don't agree with that. Let's leave that to others. They can assess the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Defence counsel's position. I would like to have counsel take the witness to his statements in the transcript and show him what he's said in the last two days that's contradictory to that, because I submit to you, with all respect, that there is nothing that's been said that's contradictory to what counsel just said. If that's counsel's position, let's go the whole way and let's go to the transcript and have counsel put these alleged contradictory answers to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, if you are saying that there is a contradiction, you should first remind him of what he said a while ago and then what he said in that other case, and then we will see whether there is a contradiction there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness mentioned these matters yesterday and today, and I think everyone can remember what he said. I have marked that part in the transcript. Unfortunately, I'm not able to find it immediately. I'd need a couple of minutes to find the relevant part in the transcript. I thought everyone could remember what the witness said, but I wanted to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could summarise the contradiction, try and remind him of the contradiction on the basis of what you yourself can remember and then we'll see what the witness has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could be of some help, Mr. President, simply just to remind you that you indeed posed a question to the gentleman today with respect to what was in the letter by the bishop. Those are the instructions. I believe that's what Mr. Kovacic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I'm referring to. Unfortunately, I can't find the relevant place in the transcript. I had marked the relevant part but I can't find it. I assumed that everyone could still remember the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me try and see these matters clearly. The contradiction concerns which part of the witness's testimony exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll find it now. It's on page 6 of today's transcript. And on page 7. Let me first remind the Chamber of what was said. The presiding Judge, Judge Antonetti, put the following question, page 6, line 2. The witness replied as follows, and it might be best if I read out what the witness answered in English. I apologise. I'll read it out in English to make sure that it's clear: [In English] "Your Honour Presiding Judge, I must correct this statement of yours because I -- it was not me who wrote that letter. That book was published as indicated in Zenica. It was written by the Zenica mufti and not by yours truly. It is true that it was published, that book, and it is true that it contains the statement which you have just now quoted. You have seen the resolution of the Muslims of Herzegovina in which we quoted provisions from both the Koran and the Prophet Mohamed on the way the war is prosecuted and the way one is to go about preserving human as well as other resources, economic resources included. You could have even noticed that it is prohibited to even destroy fruit and the fruit of fruit-bearing trees. So I can also tell you that in the bloodiest battle, which of the decisive importance for the survival of the Muslims in the first stage of the operations of the Prophet Mohamed, the so-called battle of -- and, of course, the Prophet Mohamed has to be a paragon for all of us to emulate in our lives, that is the first example of new conventional -- unconventional way of respect for human lives and prisoners." Et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And in what manner is that contradiction or a difference between what he said at that point in time and what he previously testified about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the Tuta case the answer is quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would only like to make a comment that as far as I recall, and I do not have the text itself before me, the text which you have just quoted, it continued. I mean, the statement of the witness continued, and he added something else, according to my recollections. But I cannot now read out what he further said. So I wonder if you may find also the continuation of that text which we are speaking about. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This text ends with the words, "it is possible." The witness today mentioned that it was possible. Four years ago, in a different case, his answer was completely different. His explanation was completely different. [In English] My colleague was suggesting to me that I read this sentence to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have the text in front of me and it says here -- it's on page 7, line 13: "It is also possible to ransom prisoners, and as an ultimate possibility, of course, this is just a possibility, and it is left to a discretionary decision, but, of course, when you have people who have committed massacres and various heinous crimes, but anyway it is possible that the military staff, the military court staff who are making such decisions, they may be able to mete out the death penalty in such circumstances." So the obvious contradiction is here he's saying that they can exterminate and liquidate, where in Tuta he said that these laws did not apply to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Both times under oath. Both are contradictory, clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I thank my dear colleague for helping me out because as I said in the beginning I lost the marking in the transcript. But anyway I think that the record will show that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Clarify that for us, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, everything is entirely clear here. Although I didn't see my evidence in the Tuta case in its entirety, it is possible that the thought was left uncompleted in this case, that such an instance where a court martial is established is possible in the countries where Sharia laws are applied and where Muslim laws, Islamic laws, are in place, but that something like that cannot be applied in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, the fact is that in Tuta, very clearly, in three sentences alone, you said that this entire instruction was pointless. That was your thesis. It was pointless because in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sharia laws are not implemented and the existence of Sharia laws is necessary in order to implement the instructions from that instructional booklet. If that indeed is the case, as you put it, why was that booklet then published and distributed among the members of the army? People read that book and discussed it. Why was it done that, if it was pointless and if it could not be implemented?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That segment cannot be implemented and applied. However, there are numerous passages and portions which pertain to the conduct of the soldiers who need to conduct themselves in accordance with international customs and conventions, and in no way is this text contradictory to the existing laws and rules and norms on the respect for human rights and freedoms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, this document was not brought in from another country. No. This was published in Zenica. This was published in order to be used in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1993. Why does it include, then, the portions which, as you say, may not be implemented, may not be applied?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you allow me to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, there are certain controversial things, not only in the political system but elsewhere as well. The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had a certain system and in precisely these locations where this booklet was published there existed certain forces which possibly may have affected the environment and prompted it to draft such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, I have to understand -- I have to confess that I fail to understand you. You did not explain this fully. This document was published in Zenica. Wasn't it meant to be used in the country where it was issued, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina? An average soldier that received it, and most of them were people with poor education, how would they know, how were they supposed to know, yes, this can be applied and this cannot be applied?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not allow me to complete my previous answer. These units which you treat as mujahedin units are units composed of our children, children from Mostar. This does not pertain to the mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, you accepted that in that same unit, the 7th Muslim unit, there were mujahedin members.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that in detail. There were various units active there, various corps, and other people were responsible for that. I don't have detailed information as to what relations existed between the mujahedin and the 7th Muslim unit, which was composed of Bosnian lads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You are telling us that you do not have relevant information, but you had contact, you had communication, you said that you had a power of attorney, and you were responsible for this appointment. This is contradictory in my eyes.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all, sir. The 7th Muslim Brigade was composed of members who were young men from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The man who was assistant commander for moral guidance was a theologist, and I knew him personally. I asked for advice as to how to conduct oneself under such circumstances and these were instructions or advice provided, because we had good cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You keep insisting on the fact that the mujahedin were exclusively local residents.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Not local residents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What were they, then?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mujahedin were not local residents, nationals of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, you said that.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Muslim unit was the unit which was established and made up of exclusively Bosniaks. There was not a single mujahedin among them. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You confirmed just a minute ago that the mujahedin, including foreigners, and this was a well-known fact, made up the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I think that you said this in your previous statement. This is your statement given to the investigators of the OTP on the 23rd of September, 1999, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, please allow me to intervene. Sir, in order to ensure that it's clear to everyone, can you please define for us what is a mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mujahedin are foreigners who established certain units which fought on the side of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I am now referring to the unit to which I gave a power of attorney. There wasn't a single foreign national in that unit. It was composed of exclusively local lads from Mostar, and I appointed the man who was to be in charge of their moral guidance and compliance with Islamic values. These were not mujahedin. We understand the term "mujahedin" to mean units composed of foreign nationals. I don't know enough about this, but the 7th Muslim Brigade was a unit composed of the soldiers, Muslims, of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, what relations they had with the mujahedin unit is something that I can't discuss. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, we are now going in circles. You confirmed to my first question, and it's recorded in today's transcript, you said that Karalic -- now you were talking about the power of attorney, and you said that this pertained to the 7th Muslim Brigade. You confirmed that today. And then within that unit, the 7th Muslim Brigade, there were mujahedin who were active. And you confirmed that you had given a power of attorney to the man who was to be active within that unit.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but our unit, the unit that was active in the territory of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, not Mostar.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a chance. That's absurd. Why didn't you find the document? I consulted this man as to who to appoint to that position in Mostar. This refers solely to Mostar, this document on the appointment of the chaplain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. We will put the document back. The document refers to Konjic. But let us now go back to your statement, the statement you gave on the 23rd of September, 1999. It's going to be in English. I will read this out, and you signed this statement.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Slow down, please, both of you. Please slow down, both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I really apologise, Your Honour. The problem is we are speaking the same language and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now read these two sentences in English. This is what you said. This is on page 10 of your statement, in the English version. "You asked me about the presence of mujahedin in the area. It was a war and the towns were sealed off. We were surrounded in Mostar. In our area there were not many extremist Muslim people. There were some in Konjic." [Interpretation] This explanation that you gave to us does not pertain to Mostar at all.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's impossible. I'm not as naive to talk about something that I know nothing about. You are trying deliberately to impute something to me that I didn't say. The transcript is clear -- or rather, the statement is clear. It uses the term "extremist" which is supposed to be parallel to the term "mujahedin." In our area, in Mostar, there were none. In Konjic, yes; in Central Bosnia, yes. Now, as to what relations existed between them and other units, independent units, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I don't think we need to dwell on this any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to draw to the attention of the Chamber that the witness today, on today's transcript, gave an answer to this question on page 73, line 8, and other lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now, just another issue: The instructions to the Muslim fighter. In one part of the text, there is exclusive reference to the defenders of our homeland, Bosnia and Herzegovina. So do you agree that this document was intended to the fighters of Bosnia and Herzegovina? We know that it was issued in Zenica, not in Berlin, not in Helsinki, and do you continue to affirm that this document could not have been applied in Bosnia and Herzegovina because Sharia laws are not valid in that country?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. So this document, Instructions to the Muslim Fighter, can be considered an insignificant document?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A publisher published it. This document was not accepted by the Presidency, by the army; it's just a document written by an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, I would like to go back to the instructions issued by the Zenica mufti to the soldiers of the BH army. We know that there are international standards on human rights. We know that there are Geneva Conventions and laws and customs of war. All of them stipulate that it is prohibited to kill a soldier, to subject him to humiliating treatment. However, the rules of the international law and criminal law provide certain norms that concern the perpetrators. My question is: What did this word, "liquidation" mean in the instructions of the Zenica mufti. Liquidation of prisoners, was that what was meant? I'd like to know whether within the forces existing in Bosnia and Herzegovina, there were court-martials, just like they exist in some other countries, and was there such an institution within the 7th Brigade? Was there a system that could have provided for a fair trial, if there was a need for a trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were other official documents in existence, criminal law of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as norms of the laws of war. I can tell you that this was a theory as to what options were available in Islam in relation to prisoners. However, this was not mandatory for us. This was not binding on us. Just like Koran, this document gave a theoretical idea which didn't necessarily have to be relevant for that period of time and for Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I'm not aware, and I'm sure that there were no court-martials or no summary executions, and none of that existed within the Zenica Muslim Brigade, which was a unit within the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, yesterday, on page 99 of the transcript, you say that both peoples, Muslims and Croats, were supposed to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say that in your view, the problem was that the defenders had to have symbols of both nations. You insisted several times on the symbols, saying that they had to wear the symbols of both nations.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said. I said that we insisted -- persistently insisted on agreeing on the common symbol, the common symbol that would reflect the desires of both nations, and unfortunately, agreement was not reached. A lot of energy was wasted on these symbols. People were supposed to agree on what the symbols were to be. The Muslims wanted such an agreement, and the Croats dictated to us what the symbols ought to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So based on what you say, the issue of symbols was a significant one.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Given the time when this was taking place and the circumstances at the time, it seems that the symbols were more important than the issue of defence of the town itself.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One couldn't say so. We can see from these documents that Madam Nozica put that the Muslims, or that is to say the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina accepted at their own initiative to include the symbols of the Croats in their stamps, whereas the other side didn't do the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me not have to go back to this decision of the Crisis Staff but we saw here that the legitimate representatives of the SDA, already back in early 1992, had accepted to cooperate with the HVO, first with the staff and then with the HVO, and it is quite clear that they accepted to first of all deal with the question of the aggressor, the JNA army and the Chetniks, and then to deal with relations between the two nations. It is quite clear, it emanates from it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us please move on to another topic. Can I please ask the Court usher to place a document that was already on the ELMO, or rather, is in the e-court system? It is 2D 00007. It is from the other Defence team, Madam Nozica, so if we could see it again, please. Mr. Smajkic, this is a document that you've already seen today. This is the memorandum on the situation and problems in Mostar and Bosnia and Herzegovina from September, 1992. You have spoken about it today. I would like to dwell on some of the facts in the document, elaborate a bit on it. I would like to elicit your confirmation of some things. Today we referred to the number of refugees, i.e., exiled persons, displaced persons, and you said that you couldn't remember the exact number. Can we please see -- the pages, unfortunately, are not marked but paragraph which is in the page where the top paragraph is marked by number 5, can we see that page, please. Yes. This is the page I was referring to. That is it. Thank you. You can see that this paper, at the time when it was drawn up, September, 1992, registered around 18.000 refugees, and it goes on to specify that they were from the areas of Nevesinje, Gacko, Bileca, Stolac, the Podvelezje and Dubrave villages, and also in a -- from a smaller number of towns and villages from Eastern Bosnia and Posavina. Do you agree that this number could reflect the reality?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it could. I didn't want to speak off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the inhabitants of the parts specified in this paper, from the east side, relative to Mostar - so from Stolac, from Podvelezje, from Dubrave - that these people, while fleeing the Serbian aggression, mostly all arrived in Mostar irrespective of their ethnicity. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you recall events when these people are fleeing the aggression, how they crossed over the Neretva River in boats and rafts, especially the raft near Pocitelj. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the HVO, which was in charge on behalf of both peoples of the defence and organisation of defence, analysed specifically the crossing near Pocitelj in order to reinforce that link, in order to carry over the people and care for them after they had crossed?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that. I don't know what numbers were involved, but the concentration was actually on Mostar. There couldn't have been that many people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that a good part of them, quite a few of them passed near Pocitelj?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many. I know that that took place. I'm aware of the activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you agree then that in May, after the HVO had cleansed Podvelezje and Dubrave of the aggressor and arrived at Stolac, while you were still fighting under the same standard, were these people -- did these people return to their homes for the most part? Do you know that? That is your area.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the withdrawal of the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So they returned to their homes?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you please then move on, scroll down this document, to paragraph number 6. That's the next page. At the top of the page, please. Zoom in, please. Very good. I should just like to put a question to you regarding this first introductory sentence and then later another one, just to see whether the indicated facts reflect the actual reality. The first sentence has to do with the organisation of the health system, and the first sentence states that both the housing and health facilities have been devastated, about 50 per cent being the overall level of damage. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not assert that myself with a degree of certainty. This is still a working paper. Whether it was exactly that, I can't say. This was an assumption and the paper was supposed to be further elaborated and completed, namely the Cultural Circle of Muslims was yet to state their view on that. So I cannot be sure about the extent of devastation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Due agree with that certain possible deviations this figure is more or less correct, has to be correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I shall not go into the details of the problems of the health system. I mean, the document goes on to define the other problems of the health system, et cetera, and a bit later in the text, about the middle of this text that we can see, it indicates the measures taken in the health system, saying that the dialysis centre was evacuated to Sibenik, for instance. It is underlined. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You are not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I do know that patients were transferred for treatment to Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: To Split in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This page also at the top, this subheading, or rather two pages after this one, it's paragraph number 8. Yes. That's it. Mr. Smajkic, if you take a look at this text, you will probably recall some of its content. I shall just point out for you the most important facts in it. So the first passage generally describes the damage sustained, inflicted, and so on. And then the second paragraph specifically states that on the basis of the analysis of the situation of the capacity for operation of the industrial facilities and the level of their damage, it is assessed that of perhaps 65 major enterprises in all fields, the situation was as follows: Approximately 11 were significantly damaged. I shall not go into the rest of the text. The pertaining to operations, which requires considerable resources, time and staff, and so on and so forth. And then it goes on to say that we managed to initiate production activity in about 14 enterprises with reduced capacity, in keeping with all the restrictions, and so on and so forth. And the overall impression is that the economic system, the economy, were -- was significantly damaged and that economic activity had practically died down. Do you agree with this finding?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can accept that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
