utterances.text: Can we go on to passage number 9, financing. That's good. Of relevance here, interesting to me, is the first sentence: "The beginning of war operations in the municipality of Mostar found the elected organs of government completely unprepared from the standpoint of securing monetary and credit flows in war circumstances. This lack of preparedness (whether deliberate or not) with the severance of practically all forms of communication created a situation whereby the citizens of this town, apart from being physically jeopardised by the aggressor and his artillery, also suffering a spiritual type of jeopardy." And then it goes on to say in the middle of the text: "All this has had a particular impact on payment operation flows that were severed in almost every possible direction so that they are mainly unfolding within our own and with a couple of adjacent municipalities. The consequence of this is such a situation that the Croatian dinar is the legal tender in this city, which one can earn nowhere, because even though citizens who are subject to the work obligation, to work duty, are mainly not receiving their personal incomes, have not been receiving their wages, since the 1st of June, 1992, pursuant to a decision of the war government of the HVO. The situation with pensioners is even worse. The last pensions have been paid out for March this year." And so on. So again, I'd say, an assessment which indicates a very sorry and difficult situation in the Mostar area. Would you agree in broad strokes with this picture as painted?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious, obvious from the document itself, that this was dealt with field by field, by people expert in these fields. It is obvious and it is quite certain that this is the picture as they saw from their angle. It is difficult for me to give assessments along those lines because I'm no businessman, I'm no economist, I'm not versed much in finance, but I believe that the document is to be trusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on to the next paragraph, under number 10 on the next page. It is entitled Traffic, or Transport. Can we just see the very first passage, just at the top of the page? Mr. Smajkic, let us not use up too much of our time. I should just like to draw your attention to a specific sentence and later ask you two specific questions. The most difficult situation was caused by the demolition of bridges, which precluded any possibility for the dealing with and regulation of traffic issues. The most important task in that sense is to build two bridges to link the banks of the city. So even without having to read this report, having been a resident of Mostar for so long, do you agree that after the Serbs left Mostar, all the bridges were demolished except the old bridge in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Talking about the blowing up of these principal facilities, yesterday you talked at quite some length about the blowing up of mosques and Medresas, religious schools. I myself will list for you the mosques that were demolished while the city was under the control of and shelled by the Serbian aggressor and the JNA, but as it is your particular field, I beg you to follow me. We shall no longer read this document. Mr. Smajkic is it true that the -- so while the Serbs were shelling the city -- so from Serbian shelling, that is, the Hajji Mehmet Bey Karagjos mosque was demolished?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just the top of the minaret of that mosque was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, I have some data that there was some other damage as well.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is possible, but it was not demolished. You asked me whether it was torn down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, you're right to criticise me. It was not a very precise question. Was it damaged?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had several holes on the roof, above the serefa part, the actual point of the minaret. It was actually damaged. But there was no major damage, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was it continued to be used for religious practices, for prayers?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because inside was some scaffolding which was set up there even prior to the aggression because work on decorating the mosque was supposed to have been executed, and so it was full of construction scaffolding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The mosque of Nesuh Aga Vucjakovic, according to the information that I have, and the images, pictures that I have, it was extensively damaged.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It only sustained minor damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Koski Mehmed-pasa mosque?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Koski Mehmed-pasa mosque also sustained some damage on the top of the minaret. We can say that it took several artillery hits but it was in a stable state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Dervis Pasa Bajezidagic mosque?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That mosque sustained major damage. And that was because it was near the Catholic church, and the Catholic church was entirely burnt. Just the walls remained. And after this aggression by the Jugo army period, we repaired it some what.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Hajji Kurta mosque?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It survived the Tabacica. It survived but it was then demolished in a second strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you say survived, to go on in this figurative vein, was it wounded severely?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot say that. It sustained certain damage but it remained standing upright.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then finally, Cose Jahija Hojja mosque, that's the last one I have information on.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that mosque only had its minaret destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since we are dealing with the destruction of these buildings, my colleague has informed me of the fact that I have missed something out. I've missed out on a document that we had. It's still on the screen, and we can see a section of this document under number 13. Yes. That's right. Beneath the question, the following paragraph starts with the word "Fact." It's a fact -- or: "The fact that the Mostar mahala centre of town were to a large extent burnt and destroyed, and that the most important cultural and religious buildings of the Muslims were destroyed or significantly damaged. In addition, there was a pre-war building that was extensive and this is -- and we have also destroyed some specific characteristics of Mostar and its centre, its most oldest parts." Yet again they are mentioning the fact that significant buildings were burnt and destroyed. Would you agree with that? We have just discussed the mosques.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That part on the left bank and the part called the mahala, the centre, those parts were exposed to direct artillery fire from the South Camp, and that is true, but you failed to mention that there were two mosques completely destroyed -- that were completely destroyed; Saric mosque and the mosque in Mahala.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was planned that we should work until quarter to 2, I believe nothing has been changed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I have another five minutes at the most, and my client will then have another ten minutes, and we can then conclude. With regard to Mr. Jaganjac, many questions were put about him. I don't want to go back to the documents. But could you provide us with one more explanation. Yesterday and today you said that Jaganjac was appointed by Tudjman. How do you know this? What's the source of your information?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this because of the contact I had with army soldiers who resisted joining the HVO and being placed under HVO command. They wanted to remain part of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Naturally, there were various aggravating circumstances that I don't want to go into.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, Witness, I'm going straight to the point.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers that I lived with said that Jasmin Jaganjac was going to be the HVO commander. They said this with joy. They really thought that all the disputes between the ABiH and the HVO would cease as a result of this appointment. He was appointed as commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to stop you but we do overlap and that causes problems for others. My question is as follows: You said that this was in the carsija in the town, that that's where he was expected or greeted in this manner.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I wanted to get the explanation that's missing in this story. You've only touched on the matter. You have no specific information from some politically authorised representative. You don't have the document on the basis of which you could draw the conclusion that the late president Tudjman appointed Jaganjac to that position. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have Mr. Jaganjac's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: He told you that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Susak, Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Jaganjac will be a witness so we'll hear about this from him. My next question that concerns Jaganjac is as follows: We saw a document according to which he was appointed by the Crisis Staff as the commander for the defence of the town. So the Crisis Staff appointed him to that post. That's stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it wasn't the Crisis Staff. It was the HVO, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, but on the basis of the Crisis Staff's authorisation.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Crisis Staff no longer existed. It had been dismantled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. We can agree on that. That's a different matter, though. But it is a fact, and we've seen the document today, that he was appointed by the Mostar HVO. Everything is done so that it seems to be legal, but I have a sufficient amount of experience to be able to claim that there is a certain background to all these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I've been informed that the witness mentioned the fact that Jaganjac -- it's 98, 8, for the sake of the transcript, Mr. Smajkic when I asked you about that, you said Tudjman and Susak. Is that correct? Tudjman or Susak.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, someone who held such a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I have to ask one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A correction to the transcript. I believe on page 98, around line 21 -- 20 or 21, the question and answer was combined in the question. I think part of that may have been Mr. Kovacic's question and part of it may have been the witness's answer. I'd just like the record to be -- transcript to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have perhaps one more minor question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said something about Croatian civilians who, in your words, HVO soldiers at the Bulevar expelled from that area of combat operations. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatian civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise; Muslim civilians.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said when the conflict broke out, you saw at the Bulevar that civilians were being expelled. I don't know in which direction.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the east, yes, I did see that. That was in the morning, early in the morning on the 9th of May, it was at dawn, and that was when this completely destructive war started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. I just wanted to be sure about that. During your testimony before the Chamber, you testified about an event when ABiH members kidnapped a Catholic priest, Don, or Father Vuksic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the right conclusion, sir. They did not kidnap him. They did not kidnap him. They were in the building -- they were in a building at the Bulevar. They had returned or taken back some of that territory. That was immediately after the 9th or 10th of May, and Mr. Vuksic was in that building. That building was destroyed as the result of HVO artillery fire, and the soldiers took him with them because they had to abandon that position, they had to return to the initial lines. They took him with them and they saved his life. Later, they handed him over through the intermediary of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you say that the army, in order to save Vuksic, took him out of this combat area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, that's my claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. I only have two other things before I conclude. Document 3D 00177 is one of the documents I want to refer to. We have the electronic version. It's a report in -- that relates to Vuksic and he recounts this event, and then the next document -- do we have that report? That's his report. I won't go any further into it. It's not necessary. He signed the document himself. His statement is somewhat different. If we follow what you said, you said that the Croatian forces were taking the civilians from that area out of the area. I'm putting it to you that the civilians were taken out of that area because of the responsibility of the army to move the civilians out of that area, and just as the army took Don Vuksic, Father Vuksic out, according to what you said.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's impossible to compare those two matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Why not? Here we have a priest and here we have a group of individuals; is that why?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we are talking -- in the first case we are talking about a priest, naturally army units or units of the ABiH were there, but in the other example, there were thousands of people who were naked, without shoes, they were expelled under fire, and I personally saw Mr. Vuksic, I know where he spent the night, and I know how ABiH forces took him with them. They came to the conclusion that it would be best to act in that way. I know that he had valuables on him, that he held on to them, and that he was provided with full security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. There are documents about that. I won't go on because my client has ten minutes to question you.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your leave --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before Mr. Praljak takes the floor, Mr. Registrar, could you calculate the time? Very well, Mr. Praljak, you may take the floor now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, in 1992, in April and May, how many soldiers did the Territorial Defence -- how many Muslim soldiers did they have in the town of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time that the Independent Mostar Battalion existed, it was composed mainly of Muslims, the HVO had nine independent battalions?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: This is not a question. Are you testifying as a witness now? You are feeding in information and not asking questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is he aware of the fact? The gentleman has been talking about facts and I asked whether there were any answers. I'm mentioning certain facts and he can say he's not aware of them, if he likes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, when there is a putsch, with the purpose of inflicting harm on another people, isn't it customary to first disarm the military forces of those people? Is that the purpose of each and any putsch?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we use the term "putsch" because these elements really were dismantled, but Mr. Praljak, there were certain acts that were carried out to the detriment of the existence of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, you know as well as I do that at the time I was the commander of that zone. Wouldn't it have been very simple for me to take one or two HVO units and to carry out a putsch by disarming the remainder of the Territorial Defence of Mostar, by declaring myself to be the commander, and by doing what you say or think that I wanted to do or that those people wanted to do. So my question is as follows: How is it possible that one unit, 120 men strong, in May, 1992, and in July we had a brigade composed mostly of Muslims, and in November, 1992, we had ABiH Corps, and then one year later, the conflict broke out, we won't go into that, but the intention, our intention was always for the entire corps to -- is it true to say that the entire corps grew?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That part is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Since you mentioned Jaganjac, who led the attack from the right bank to the left bank in Mostar in the month of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO, together with the army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The person.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jasmin Jaganjac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at that time, Jasmin Jaganjac was not even in Mostar? Are you aware of the fact?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So would you say that you could describe yourself as a well-informed man, if you're not aware of the identity of the commander of the most important military element in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I had a meet with Mr. Jaganjac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. Have you shown to the Chamber photographs of the mosques and other religious buildings that were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time ask anyone for an expert report on the way in which mosques and other religious buildings were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was done last year. The most prominent experts, engineers from all these fields did this, and they determined the state of the religious buildings with precision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you requested that a report be compiled on the way in which those buildings had been destroyed. Did you ask for a ballistics report, an analysis of the explosives used?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you ever request that an investigation be carried out by the legal organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina with regard to the way in which the religious buildings in Mostar were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Was that investigation ever brought to an end?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It hasn't been concluded yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Are you aware of the fact that in Suica, and you said that there were no conflicts between the Muslims and the Croats there, are you aware of how far away from Suica there were fights with the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could make a guess. I don't know the exact distance but, no, I don't know exactly, but I know where that place is. It's difficult for me to provide you with the exact distance.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, yesterday, why did you repeat on two occasions that there were no conflicts between the Muslims and Croats in Suica but you failed to mention what you're now saying, namely that you know that there was a fierce fight between the Croats and Chetniks in the immediate vicinity of Suica?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm focusing on the mosques, but as for the conflict between the Chetniks and these others, well, that's not what I'm interested in at this point in time. I didn't pass over that in silence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Failing to mention important fact demonstrates that you want to claim that that mosque was destroyed for the sole reason that this is what the Croats want. You don't want to say that it was possible for this to be destroyed, for this mosque to be destroyed by the Chetniks in the course of the fight against the Chetniks. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Suica and those who lived in the vicinity of the mosque informed me of the identity of those who had destroyed the mosque, so it's not necessary for me to expand on this story.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When you mention the fact that the Muslims were in the HVO, because of their salaries and some sort of parcels, did you receive or were you given any statements from these people according to which they remained in the HVO because of their salaries and the parcels they received? Do you have such statements and have you brought such statements here with you?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any such written statements.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I have understood you, in the case of those who told you about how the mosque was destroyed, in the case of the soldiers, well you took no statements from these people, you are just interpreting what these people told you. And this interpretation has no probative value here. What were the salaries like in the HVO in April and May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did the salaries amount to 30 German marks, or 15 euros, for 15 days at the front?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. We mentioned the 4th Brigade, the Muderiz 4th Brigade which was part of the 4th Corps, and we talked about its composition in the area that you were the mufti of.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When this brigade was lined up, was the greeting as follows: "Who are you fighting for?" One of them would ask such a question. And the troops would reply: "For Allah." And then this person would ask, "Who are you fighting against?" And they would answer, "Against the Vlahs." And this was repeated three times. Tell me, are the "Vlahs" those who are not Muslims; the Catholics and Orthodox?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a colloquial expression.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Is such a religious bias on the part of that unit and all other units in which Emirs were appointed related exclusively to the concept of mujahedin, and in all dictionaries, in the Encyclopedia Britannica, in the Larousse encyclopaedia this term is defined as a religious fighter, a fighter in a holy war.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those units did not support such a symbol or such a slogan.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We have seen here that an entire brigade would say, "For Allah," not, "For Bosnia and Herzegovina," not for a secular state. Not for what you have been discussing here. They would say, "For Allah." All units in which Emirs had been appointed acted in this way. My question is: Was there a single soldier in such units --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to object at this point. I know Mr. Praljak is not a lawyer but questions have to be put properly in any event. What Mr. Praljak has done repeatedly in the last ten minutes has make long statements, there is no answer to the statement, and then he puts another question which may or may not relate to the assertion Mr. Praljak made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your last question now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: My last question: Were there any Muslim units in which there was a member who was not a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many such units.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And which Muslim unit? The 7th Muslim unit, the El Mujahid unit, the Muderiz unit, et cetera, in which such unit was there a member who was not a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One would have to prepare to answer such a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have concluded my cross-examination. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now adjourn for the week. I'd like to provide you with some information about the time that has been used up. So far, as far as the cross-examination is concerned, two hours and 49 minutes have been used up, so two hours and 50 minutes, and that leaves you with five hours for your cross-examination. I'd like to remind you of the fact that the Prosecution took up three hours and 58 minutes, almost four hours, and Judges' questions and certain other interventions took up almost 102 minutes. The total time used for this witness amounts to eight hours and 29 minutes so far, and we have not yet finished. Mr. Kovacic, let's have the numbers very rapidly, given the fact that time is short.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We are asking for admission of only one document, the last one which was put on the system. It is number 3D 00177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. This exhibit will be therefore tendered and admitted with today's date as 3D 00177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sir, I wish you a good return to Mostar. Since you have a full schedule as of tomorrow up until Monday, we invite you to return on Wednesday because you'll be testifying here on Wednesday and for a certain period of time on Thursday. Mrs. Nozica, as far as your exhibits are concerned. Yes, very well, then, Mr. Registrar could you deal with these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Admitted with today's date. We have: 2D 00012, 2D 00013, 2D 00016, 2D 00018, 2D 00021, 2D 00022, 2D 00024. The following exhibits are marked for identification pending translation. These are: 2D 00025, 2D 00026, 2D 00028. I also note that a previously admitted exhibit is still waiting translation and therefore is still marked for identification and not admitted, and this is 2D 00007. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I hope you all have good rest and we will resume with the hearings on Monday at 2.15 p.m..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of May, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
